t: A temple town in Peru’s Ancash highlands, c. 950–400 BCE, whose priests drew pilgrims and offerings from the coast, mountains and forests.
Its stone galleries hid the Lanzón, a carved granite god, and its art of jaguars, eagles and caimans spread far across Peru.
It held sway through religion rather than armies; after its decline regional cultures such as Paracas developed their own styles.
dyk: In 2001 archaeologists found twenty decorated trumpets made from conch shells, brought from the seas off Ecuador, hidden in a small gallery beside the temple’s Circular Plaza.
ev: A temple settlement is founded at Chavín de Huántar, on Richard Burger’s revised dates
The U-shaped Old Temple and the Lanzón gallery form the heart of the cult
In the Janabarriu phase the town grows to some 42 hectares and Chavín art spreads widely
The ceremonial centre is abandoned; a village later grows over the old plaza
Julio C. Tello begins work at the site and calls Chavín the mother culture of the Andes
A debris flow buries much of the site and the modern town under mud
Chavín de Huántar is inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site

f.predecessor: Initial Period temple centres of the central Andes
f.successor: Huarás culture; later the Recuay culture
